items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I recorded with Buck and his band the 23rd of November, 1949, which included a French personal of Alix Combelle (tenor sax) Armand Conrad (tenor sax), George Kennedy (alto-sax), André Persiany (piano), George Hadjo(bass).

ctx.x: When I came back to Paris near the end of September, I contacted a West Indian drummer named George Smith whom I had met before and asked him about joining the orchestra for the Chikito as a drummer was the only musician missing in the line-up. He accepted and I wrote to "Bass" Hill and asked him to start collecting some music in New York. When I received an answer from him, he told me not to worry about music because Norman Lester was an arranger and would take care of the repertoire.

Buck Clayton had come to Paris with an orchestra which included Merrill Stepter, a trumpetist I had known a long time and Wallace Bishop the drummer. I recorded with Buck and his band the 23rd of November, 1949, which included a French personal of Alix Combelle (tenor sax) Armand Conrad (tenor sax), George Kennedy (alto-sax), André Persiany (piano), George Hadjo(bass).

We did six numbers in which one featured the three trumpets on "Sweet Georgia Brown" and one featured Buck and I on a number we called B.C. and B.C. and it's very easy to see the connection between the title and the two of us.

items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The pianist was Andre Persiany who was known as the French Milt Buckner. We called him Pepe. ... I had been working with these musicians for a few months, we decided to use them for the tour

ctx.x: I had the privilege of going out of the club now and then to do ates in different places and that was the way I worked until February of 1956. In October 1955, I played a two days jazz festival in Lyon which featured Sydney Bechet, Chet Baker and myself. Sidney was the main attraction because his popularity had grown immensely since 1950 and he was the biggest crowd drawing jazz musician in Europe. At one time, I didn't dig him mostly I suppose because I didn't like the sound of soprano saxophone. But I dug him…

The musicians that accompanied me at the Trois Maillets were Michel de Villers, whom I had made my first tour with as a member of the Edouard's band. He was now playing alto and baritone sax. The pianist was Andre Persiany who was known as the French Milt Buckner. We called him Pepe. My friend Guy Lafitte was on tenor. There was Paul Rovere, a fine young bass player and Jappy Gauthier on drums. Lily had been working on another tour of France for a few months and as the club was going to close for the
month of February and I had been working with these musicians for a few months, we decided to use them for the tour with Cecily Forde as the canary.
